text: Mostly because we've got used to instant results. Food, films and even taxis arrive within minutes, so any delay feels like a failure of the system rather than a normal part of life. Social media makes it worse, since it trains us to expect a reaction the moment we post something. As a result, waiting in a queue or for a reply now seems much longer than it really is.

tips.en: Mostly because … gives the answer in the first words.
tips.ru: Mostly because … — ответ в первых словах.
tips.example: Mostly because we've got used to instant results

tips.en: As a result … draws a conclusion from the examples.
tips.kk: As a result … — мысалдардан шыққан қорытынды.
tips.ru: As a result … — вывод из примеров.
tips.example: As a result, waiting in a queue

questions.question: Why do many people find it hard to be patient nowadays?

text: I'd say it's one of the most useful things parents can teach. Children who learn to wait for a reward usually cope better at school, because real learning takes time and effort. It doesn't have to be strict — simple things like saving pocket money for a toy or growing vegetables in the garden show them that the best results rarely come immediately.

tips.en: One of the most useful things states a clear position from the start.
tips.kk: One of the most useful things — алғашқы сөздерден анық ұстаным.
tips.ru: One of the most useful things — ясная позиция с первых слов.
tips.example: one of the most useful things parents can teach

tips.en: Saving pocket money and growing vegetables are concrete methods, not general words.
tips.kk: Saving pocket money, growing vegetables — жалпы сөздің орнына нақты тәсілдер.
tips.ru: Saving pocket money, growing vegetables — конкретные способы вместо общих слов.
tips.example: saving pocket money for a toy

questions.question: Is it important to teach children to wait?

text: Reducing waiting times is obviously important, but not at any cost. If doctors are pushed to see patients faster and faster, the quality of care will suffer, and mistakes become more likely. I think a better approach is to be honest about waiting times and use online booking, so people can plan their day instead of sitting in a corridor for hours.

tips.en: Obviously important, but not at any cost balances the position.
tips.kk: Obviously important, but not at any cost — ұстанымның теңгерімі.
tips.ru: Obviously important, but not at any cost — баланс позиции.
tips.example: Reducing waiting times is obviously important, but not at any cost

tips.en: A better approach is … proposes a way out.
tips.kk: A better approach is … — жауап шешім ұсынады.
tips.ru: A better approach is … — ответ предлагает выход.
tips.example: I think a better approach is to be honest about waiting times

questions.followUp: What would be a fair waiting time?
questions.question: Should public services, such as hospitals, try to reduce waiting times at any cost?

text: In some ways, yes. My grandparents waited years for a flat or a telephone line, and they simply accepted it because there was no alternative. But I'm not sure that was real patience — it was more a lack of choice. Today people complain more, but that pressure has also forced many companies and services to improve, which is not necessarily a bad thing.

tips.en: Not real patience but a lack of choice reframes the question itself.
tips.kk: Not real patience — it was more a lack of choice — жауап сұрақтың өзін қайта қарайды.
tips.ru: Not real patience — it was more a lack of choice — ответ пересматривает сам вопрос.
tips.example: it was more a lack of choice

tips.en: Not necessarily a bad thing shows the other side of impatience.
tips.kk: Not necessarily a bad thing — шыдамсыздықтың екінші жағы.
tips.ru: Not necessarily a bad thing — вторая сторона нетерпения.
tips.example: which is not necessarily a bad thing

questions.followUp: Why do you think that is?
questions.question: Do you think people were more patient in the past?

text: I think in the long run it probably is. Talent gives you a good start, but most people who reach the top in sport, science or business have spent years practising things that nobody noticed. Many talented people give up when progress slows down. So patience, or persistence, is often what separates those who succeed from those who simply showed promise.

tips.en: In the long run it probably is gives an opinion without being absolute.
tips.kk: In the long run it probably is — кесімсіз пікір.
tips.ru: In the long run it probably is — мнение без категоричности.
tips.example: in the long run it probably is

tips.en: What separates those who succeed … sums up the answer in one sentence.
tips.kk: What separates those who succeed … — бір сөйлемдегі қорытынды.
tips.ru: What separates those who succeed … — вывод в одной фразе.
tips.example: what separates those who succeed from those who simply showed promise
